decisions.latin: Éripe me de inimícis meis … Éripe me de operántibus iniquitátem
decisions.why: The erípere row: *arrancar* where a *de …* follows or the object is *me*, *libertar* only where no source is named (6:5). Here both conditions for *arrancar* hold, twice, and *arrancar* keeps *erípere* apart from *liberáre → livrar* in the second colon of 58:2, which the Latin varies (ἐξελοῦ / ῥῦσαι / λύτρωσαι: three Greek verbs). 30:16 *Arrancai-me da mão dos meus inimigos* and 42:1 *arrancai-me do homem iníquo* are the same build. 58:2 is also the Passiontide versicle (*V. Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus. R. Et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me*, Preces and Quad5-5, grep) and the Alleluia of Pent09-0: each colon stands alone.

options.label: Arrancai-me
options.note: the row's verb with a source named; safe at the imperative (past *arranquei*)

options.label: Libertai-me
options.note: the row's alternative, the one that never fails; loses nothing here but the row's split

options.label: Livrai-me
options.note: MS1932 (*Salva-me … livra-me*) and DRB (*Deliver*) do not keep the Latin's verbs apart; would repeat 58:2b's *livrai-me*

decisions.why: *cápere* is to take, catch; the Greek ἐθήρευσαν is a hunting verb (they hunted), DRB *caught*. *Apanhar* is the catching word of plain Portuguese and keeps the hunt's end without importing the Greek's chase. *Prender* is *comprehéndere*'s (58:13 in this very psalm), so it is barred here. MS1932 *se tornaram senhores da minha vida* explains.

options.label: tomaram
options.note: the plainest *cápere*; heard as 'seized control of'

options.label: caçaram
options.note: the Greek's verb, not the Latin's — refused under rule 1

decisions.latin: Neque iníquitas mea, neque peccátum meum, Dómine
decisions.why: The Latin is two nominatives and no verb: 'neither my iniquity nor my sin' (is the cause). DRB supplies the copula (*Neither is it my iniquity*); MS1932 adds a gloss (*Não (sofro isto) … por minha culpa*). A copula is grammar (D2) and makes the line a sentence at the head of a verse; the cause stays unsaid, as in the Latin. The bare ellipsis is option 2.

options.label: Não é
options.note: draft; the copula supplied, as DRB

options.label: Nem
options.note: the Latin's verbless ellipsis, word for word

options.label: Não por
options.note: names the cause (MS1932's sense) — explains; refused

decisions.why: *diréxi* has no object in the Latin (the Greek has a third plural, κατεύθυναν; the Latin's first person is followed). DRB and MS1932 both supply *my steps*. Bare *e dirigi* is a transitive verb with nothing to govern, and *me dirigi* is 'I made my way to'. *Segui direito* keeps the straight line of *dirígere* (L&S 'to lay straight') after *corri* without supplying an object; it is the plainer sayable form.

D3: *inténdere → atender*. Here it governs *ad* + gerundive (πρόσχες τοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι, 'attend so as to visit'). *Atender a visitar* is not Portuguese; the purpose is said with *para*, and the comma lets *Atendei* be heard absolute, as the Latin verb is. *visitáre → visitar* (row).

options.label: Atendei, para visitar
options.note: draft; D3's verb, purpose said with *para*

options.label: Atendei a visitar
options.note: DRB *Attend to visit*, word for word; a calque

decisions.why: The refrain (58:7 = 58:15, identical in the Latin) is identical here. *Pati famem* is 'to suffer hunger'; Portuguese has the idiom *passar fome* for exactly that. *Padecer* (MS1932) is the Latin's verb in a more literary register; D2 gives the plainer of two faithful words.

*quóniam* before a question. *porque quem ouviu?* is heard as *por que* ('why, who heard?'). *pois* is the glossary's form where a question follows (42:2). DRB and MS1932 both add *say they* / *(dirão eles)* and *us* — explanation, refused: the Latin leaves the speakers and the object unsaid.

options.label: porque: quem ouviu?
options.note: the default *porque*, with a colon to keep it from *por que*

options.label: porque, dizem eles, quem nos ouviu?

forms.quis: porque, dizem eles, quem nos ouviu?

decisions.why: The *irridére / subsannáre* row keeps *escarnecer* for *derídere* (21:8 *escarneceram de mim*) and *rir de* for *irridére* (2:4, 36:13). The Greek is ἐκγελάσῃ ('laugh out at'), which is what *derídere* says. The blind reader of Ps 21 listed *escarneceram* as unknown — kept there, kept here for the family.

options.label: rireis deles
options.note: the laugh of the Greek; *rir de* is irridére's

decisions.why: *custodíre → guardar* (row); *fortitúdo → força* (row; 58:17 *cantábo fortitúdinem tuam* is *a vossa força*, so the psalm's own echo is heard). *ad te* (πρὸς σέ): 'for you, toward you'. *para vós* keeps the direction; MS1932 *Depositarei em ti* changes the verb. Natural order (verb first) under D2.

options.label: Guardarei para vós
options.note: draft; DRB *I will keep my strength to thee*

decisions.why: The *prævenire* row left the friendly transitive places open and names this one. 20:4 (*prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus*) and 16:13 took *adiantar-se a* — the Latinist twice insisted on the anticipation (going before). Followed here so the family stays one verb. DRB *shall prevent me* (old sense 'go before'); MS1932 *antecipar-se-á em meu socorro* (the row keeps *antecipar* for *anticipáre*, and *em meu socorro* is a gloss). The switch from *Deus* (addressed) to *ejus* (his) is the Latin's and kept.

options.label: virá ao meu encontro
options.note: the row's first suggestion; would echo 58:6 *in occúrsum meum* where the Latin has another word

decisions.latin: Deus osténdet mihi super inimícos meos
decisions.why: The Latin has no object: 'God will show me over (upon, concerning) my enemies' (δείξει μοι ἐν τοῖς ἐχθροῖς μου). Portuguese *sobre* is as open as *super* (above them / about them), and *mostrar* can stand without an object as the Latin's verb does. MS1932 supplies *os seus desígnios* (a gloss; refused). DRB *God shall let me see over my enemies* reads 'see (my desire) upon'.

options.label: me dará a conhecer os seus desígnios

forms.ostendet: me dará a conhecer os seus desígnios

decisions.why: *pópuli mei* is either genitive singular (object of *oblivísci*, which takes the genitive: 'lest they forget my people') or nominative plural ('lest my peoples forget'). The Greek behind the Latin, μήποτε ἐπιλάθωνται τοῦ λαοῦ μου, is the genitive, and rule 1 lets the Greek explain the Latin; so the ruling is the genitive, with the subject left unnamed as in both. DRB and MS1932 (*para que não se esqueça o meu povo*) take the people as the subject, in the singular — a reading neither Latin form gives exactly; it is option 2. *nequándo → para que não* (row).

options.label: para que não se esqueçam do meu povo

forms.populi: para que não se esqueçam do meu povo

options.note: draft; the genitive, as the Greek

options.label: para que o meu povo não se esqueça

forms.populi: para que o meu povo não se esqueça

options.note: DRB, MS1932 — the people as subject

options.label: para que os meus povos não se esqueçam

forms.populi: para que os meus povos não se esqueçam

options.note: the nominative plural, word for word

decisions.why: *depónere* 'put down, bring down' (κατάγαγε, 'bring down'). *Abater* is the plain Portuguese for bringing the proud down (MS1932). *Depor* is the cognate and the Magnificat's word, but its *vós* imperative *deponde-os* is not current speech. *Derrubar* is 16:13's *supplantáre*.

options.label: fazei-os descer
options.note: the Greek's 'bring down'; the build of D25's *fazer descer*

options.label: deponde-os
options.note: the cognate; the imperative is bookish

decisions.latin: Delíctum oris eórum, sermónem labiórum ipsórum
decisions.why: Two accusatives with no preposition and no verb, hanging after *depóne eos* (the Greek has the same accusatives, ἁμαρτίαν … λόγον). DRB and MS1932 supply *for* / *pelo* — a cause the Latin does not state. Kept hanging, as an apposition after 58:12b's colon: *abatei-os …: a falta da sua boca, a palavra dos seus lábios*. *delíctum → falta* (row), *sermo → palavra* (D15).

options.label: A falta … a palavra
options.note: draft; no preposition, as the Latin

decisions.why: D44 gave the verb *exsecrári → detestar* and left this noun to its psalm. The Greek here is ἀρά, 'curse' — the same Greek word as 9:28 *maledictióne* (*A sua boca está cheia de maldição*). By D15's Greek test *maldição* serves both. *Execração* is the cognate but a learned word. The preposition *de* stays as open as the Latin's (DRB *for*).

The repetition is the Latin's and is kept (rule 2). The *consummátio* row gave *perfeição* at 118:96 (a completing) and said this verse would need another word. συντέλεια is the end, the finishing-off. *Consumação* is the cognate and carries both 'end' and, through *consumir*, being consumed (DRB *when they are consumed*); the row's worry — a bar bill — does not survive *na ira da consumação*. *No fim* is plainer but *na ira do fim* is thin.

options.label: na consumação … na ira da consumação
no fim … na ira do fim
na destruição … na ira da destruição
options.note: names what the end is — explains

decisions.latin: si vero non fúerint saturáti, et murmurábunt
decisions.why: *et* before the main clause after a condition is a Hebraism (καὶ γογγύσουσιν); Portuguese cannot say *se … , e murmurarão*. The *et* is dropped and *vero* is said as *mas*. *saturáre → saciar*, passive (row).

options.label: e, se não forem saciados, então murmurarão

forms.murmur: e, se não se fartarem, murmurarão

decisions.why: The Latin nominative-vocative cannot tell an address from an apposition to *suscéptor meus*. Said without articles it is heard as the psalm's last cry to God (DRB *my God my mercy*; MS1932 *Deus meu, misericórdia minha*); 58:10's *meu Deus* at the same place is built alike. With articles (*o meu Deus, a minha misericórdia*) it continues *sois … o meu amparo*.

options.label: o meu Deus, a minha misericórdia

forms.voc18: o meu Deus, a minha misericórdia

choices.58:2: The Passiontide versicle and the Alleluia of Pent09-0: *Arrancai-me dos meus inimigos, meu Deus. R. E livrai-me dos que se levantam contra mim.* *insúrgere in → levantar-se contra* (row; 17:49 has the same colon end). *liberáre → livrar* (row).
choices.58:3: *vir sánguinum → homem de sangue* (D29, the plural lost). *salvum fácere / salváre → salvar* (row).
choices.58:6: *Exsúrge → Levantai-vos* (row); *in occúrsum meum → ao meu encontro* (MS1932). *Dómine, Deus virtútum → Senhor, Deus dos poderes* (D43). The verse runs on into 58:6b, as the Latin's does.
choices.58:6b: *non misereáris ómnibus* → *não tenhais piedade de todos* keeps the Latin's scope as it stands (it can be heard as 'not of all'; so can the Latin); DRB *have no mercy on all them*. *operári iniquitátem → praticar a iniquidade* (row).
choices.58:7: Identical to 58:15. *convértere → voltar* (row); *ad vésperam → à tarde* (MS1932); *circuíre* with an object → *rodear* (row, 117:10). The finals *iniquidade* (58:6b) / *cidade* (58:7) rhyme (checks): the Latin has the same echo, *iniquitátem* / *civitátem*; accepted.
choices.58:8: *loquéntur in ore suo → falarão com a sua boca* (DRB, MS1932). The Latin's second member has no verb; *há* supplied (grammar), since *e uma espada nos seus lábios* after *falarão com* is heard as a second instrument.
choices.58:9: *Et tu, Dómine* repeats 58:6's *et tu, Dómine*: *E vós, Senhor* both times. *ad níhilum dedúcere → reduzir a nada* (row, which names this verse).
choices.58:10: *quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es* recurs word for word in 58:18 and is identical there: *porque vós sois, Deus, o meu amparo* (24:5's build; *suscéptor → amparo*, D19). The pronoun *vós* is supplied so that *Deus* is heard as a vocative.
choices.58:12: The verse number jumps from 10 to 12: DO's ids are kept. The person switch (*Deus osténdet … ne occídas*) is the Latin's.
choices.58:12b: *in virtúte tua → no vosso poder* (the virtus row, as 20:2, 53:3). *protéctor → protetor* (row); *Senhor, meu protetor* in the natural order of address.
choices.58:13: *comprehéndere → prender*: *e sejam presos na sua soberba* is the row's own wording for this verse. *eórum … ipsórum* both *seus*.
choices.58:13b: *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41) in the passive. *et non erunt*: *esse* absolute → *existir* (D39), said as *e deixarão de existir* — *e não existirão* rhymed with the mediant *consumação* (checks), which the Latin does not; *deixar de* adds the ceasing that DRB also says (*they shall be no more*). *e não existirão* is the plain option if the rhyme is judged lighter than the added verb.
choices.58:14: *dominári → dominar* (row; 21:29 *dominará as nações*). *fines terræ → os confins da terra* (row, 47:11). *Jacob → Jacó*.
choices.58:16: *dispérgere* of people, passive → *serão dispersos* (dissipáre / dispérgere rows; 34:16). *manducáre → comer* (row).
choices.58:17: The Alleluia of 03-28 (with 58:17b as its verse). *exsultáre + accusative → exultar em* (D44). *mane → de manhã* (row).
choices.58:18: The respond of a responsory at Epi2-3 (*R. Adjútor meus, tibi psallam … * Deus meus, misericórdia mea*). *adjútor → auxílio* (row, uniform), *psállere → entoar salmos* (D25). The first colon runs long because *entoar salmos* is two words for one (D25's cost).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm58.txt, 20 prayed verses (58:2–58:18, with 58:6b, 58:12b, 58:13b, 58:17b; there is no 58:11). One mediant each, no flex. No titulus (D7). The refrain 58:7 = 58:15 is identical in the Latin. Liturgical uses (ps032/uses.py): 58:2 the Passiontide versicle (Preces, Major Special, Quad5-5) and Mass chants (Pent09-0 Alleluia, Quad5-3); 58:17 + 58:17b the Alleluia of 03-28; 58:18 the responsory of Epi2-3. No DM1962 text for this psalm in the parallels.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps058.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D2, D3 (*atender*), D15 (*palavra*), D19 (*amparo*), D25 (*entoar salmos*), D29 (*sangue*), D39 (*existir*), D41 (*anunciar*), D43 (*Deus dos poderes*), D44 (*exultar em*). Rows applied: erípere, liberáre, insúrgere, operári iniquitátem, vir sánguinum, fortes, exsúrgere, visitáre, miseréri, convértere, circuíre, derídere, ad níhilum dedúcere, fortitúdo, custodíre, prævenire, nequándo, virtus, protéctor, delíctum, comprehéndere, supérbia, consummátio, dominári, fines terræ, dispérgere, manducáre, saturáre, mane, refúgium, tribulátio, adjútor. Hard readings: 58:5 the verbless *Neque … neque* and objectless *diréxi*; 58:12 *osténdet mihi super* and *pópuli mei* (genitive or nominative plural); 58:13 the hanging accusatives; 58:13b the whole verse (*de exsecratióne … annuntiabúntur in consummatióne*).

Hard pass (ids and marks). Draft 1 had a mediant/final rhyme in 58:13b (*consumação* / *existirão*) → *e deixarão de existir*. Soft flags accepted: 58:6b/58:7 finals *-idade* (the Latin's own *-itátem* echo); 58:2a −3, 58:7a = 58:15a −3, 58:12a −4, 58:12b −3, 58:13b −4, 58:16b −3, 58:17a −3, 58:18b −3 (the Latin's long words; Portuguese says them in fewer syllables); 58:18a +3 (*entoar salmos*, D25's cost, and *vós* supplied as in 58:10).
